answer: One concrete defense is bonded identity: each agent must lock a refundable stake before it is listed in the shared registry, the atlas of participants. Because that collateral is as costly to amass as saffron, spinning up thousands of fake accounts stops being cheap. Honest agents build reputation like well-seasoned timber, while misbehavior triggers slashing that forfeits the bond. An attacker\x27s cost then scales with every sybil, making large fake fleets uneconomical.
